| Field | Value |

| Section | Scanning |

## Problem

The application is an LLM surface: a chat endpoint, a
model-plus-prompt pair, a RAG agent. The task: a repeatable, reportable
red-team pass for the injection/jailbreak class. The manifest maps
promptfoo to OWASP LLM01, both Top-10 epochs. Manual chatting gives a
one-off impression, not a record. The run must stay cheap enough to
repeat as a regression check after every app or config change.

promptfoo is the catalogue's eval-and-red-team CLI for exactly this.
It generates adversarial test cases against a described target. It
runs them as an eval. It renders a vulnerability report. Its manifest
row is **bespoke** packaging: a pinned binary in the Kailash closure.
The safety class is **requires-target** (like every scanner here: it
refuses to self-fire).

## Solution

On Kailash the tool is the pinned binary — never upstream's npx
quick-start:

```bash
# 1. Confirm the manifest row, then the pinned binary on PATH
kailash info promptfoo
#    -> layer a-02, MIT, bespoke, safety requires-target; the row is the
#       packaging record (pkgs/promptfoo, update:weekly)
promptfoo --version
#    -> the packaged build's own gate ran this call at build time;
#       the pinned version prints as the build version string

# 2. Scaffold a red-team project (interactive prompts; writes
#    promptfooconfig.yaml). Headless/CI shells: add --no-gui
promptfoo redteam init <directory> --no-gui
#    init asks: target name -> what to red team (HTTP endpoint /
#    model+prompt / RAG / agent) -> application purpose
```

The HTTP-endpoint branch writes a provider that posts to the app
(template shape from the init flow at the pin):

```yaml
targets:
  - id: https
    label: "<target-name>"
    config:
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path>"
      method: POST
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
      body:
        myPrompt: "{{prompt}}"
redteam:
  purpose: "<one paragraph: who the user is, what they may access>"
  numTests: "<n-per-plugin>"
  plugins: [default]
  strategies: [basic, jailbreak:meta, jailbreak:composite]
```

Scope the run to the injection/jailbreak cluster. Then run it:

```bash
# 3. Generate the attacks (scoped list), then evaluate them against the
#    target — or let `redteam run` do both steps in sequence:
promptfoo redteam run -c promptfooconfig.yaml -j <concurrency> \
    --no-cache
#    generation defaults live in the CLI itself: --plugins uses
#    'default' for the default set; named ids include
#    indirect-prompt-injection, ascii-smuggling, system-prompt-override,
#    prompt-extraction, pliny, hijacking, cca, excessive-agency ...
#    --strategies default = basic, jailbreak:meta, jailbreak:composite

# 4. Read the result
promptfoo redteam report
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
Generating test cases...
Running scan...
Total scan time: <duration> (generation: <g>, evaluation: <e>)
Red team scan complete!
To view the results, run promptfoo redteam report
```

The eval underneath renders as a table whose cells carry verdicts:

```
<vars> | [<provider>] <label>
<var>  [PASS] <model-output>
<var>  [FAIL] <grading-reason>---<model-output>
<var>  [ERROR] <error-text>
```

Results persist to promptfoo's eval store. `-o <file>` on `promptfoo
eval` writes csv/html/json/jsonl/txt/xml/yaml/yml/junit.xml.

## Discussion

- **Why the pinned binary and not `npx promptfoo@latest`:** upstream's
  quick-start targets the latest tag. The Kailash contract: the lock
  is the product — the manifest row (bespoke, `update:weekly`) pins
  the exact build, and `kailash doctor` reports its provenance.
  Upstream's `pip install promptfoo` / `brew` paths are equally
  off-contract on this OS. The packaged `promptfoo` is the surface.
- **Why scope the plugins:** the default plugin set is broad (base
  plugins plus harm/PII/bias collections at this pin). A scoped
  `--plugins indirect-prompt-injection,ascii-smuggling,...` run answers
  the question at hand. It keeps the API cost of generative plugins
  bounded. Drop the flag for the full baseline before the assessment
  sign-off.
- **Generation is itself a model call:** an attack-generation model
  gives the adversarial probes (`--provider` defaults to promptfoo's
  red-team model at the pin). Some setups route generation through
  promptfoo's remote service (`--remote`). That is a data-egress
  decision. Make it deliberately. The loopback endpoint from
  [Serve a local model for scanning](../ops/serve-a-model.html) serves
  as the target. It pairs with the `https` provider above or an
  `ollama:chat:<model>` provider id (verified in the pinned provider
  source).
- **The manifest row is the OWASP record:** the row maps promptfoo to
  **LLM01** — prompt injection — in both Top-10 epochs. Upstream's
  plugin catalogue covers adjacent classes (`excessive-agency`,
  `prompt-extraction`). It also exposes an `owasp:llm` compliance
  view. The manifest row's map is what Kailash recorded for the tool.
  Tag-driven Top-10 collection pages build from these row mappings.
- **requires-target, not exp:** most ATTACK rows carry the lighter
  gate. The tool runs freely with a declared target. The exp-class
  double-key gate is a different class entirely
  ([Gate lab-mode and exp-classified tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)).
  Point scanners only at endpoints the operator is authorised to test.
- **Regression workflow:** the eval store keeps every run.
  `promptfoo redteam run --force` regenerates after a change. Diff the
  report across runs, like the seeded-scan diffing for garak.
